sections.h2: Which Nash County office sends and collects the tax bill?
sections.html:
One combined office serves as both assessor and collector in Nash County. It lists and values real and personal property, assesses it and collects the resulting tax. Find it at 120 W. Washington St., Suite 2058, Nashville, NC 27856, and you can call 252-459-9824 during the business day, which runs from 8 a.m. to 5 p.m.

Relief applications under state law also go through this office. The Collections page explains that the collector handles money, while questions about listing, billing and assessed values belong with the assessor's staff.

The county commissioners adopt the rate in spring, by June 30 at the latest, and a bill multiplies that rate by each $100 of taxable value. Mailing happens in July or August. An owner with no statement by September 15 should call the collector.

sections.h2: How do Nash County's numbers compare on housing?
sections.html:
The Census Bureau puts Nash County at roughly 99,365 people in mid-2025, up 4.6% from its 2020 base. The land area is 540.44 square miles, and the county held close to 176 residents for each one in 2020.

  • Half of owner-occupied homes are worth more than $191,000 (2020-2024).
  • Households owning their home: 63.6%.
  • Typical monthly rent: $953.
  • Total homes and apartments by mid-2025: 45,068.
  • Average trip to a job: 23.7 minutes.
  • Veterans among residents (2020-2024): 5,784.

Since 63.6% of households own, a meaningful share of Nash County houses are rentals. A landlord should remember that the county bills whoever owns the parcel on January 1, whatever the tenant pays.

sections.h2: What dates and penalties apply to a Nash County tax bill?
sections.html:
Bills come due September 1 and stay payable through January 5, according to the county. If January 5 is a Saturday or Sunday, payment is accepted through the following working day. A postmark by the deadline counts, though the county suggests mailing at least five business days ahead.

Past-due realty and personal property accounts pick up 2% for January and then 0.75% for each later month, which tracks G.S. 105-360. Registered motor vehicles are handled separately, at 5% for the first month past due.

  • Delinquent real estate may be advertised in local papers between March 1 and June 30, with the advertising cost charged to the owner.
  • The tools on the county's list: garnishing wages, attaching bank accounts or rents, foreclosure, and offsetting state income tax refunds.
  • Prepayments toward a coming bill are accepted, and the office can explain the terms.

sections.h2: Who pays the Nash County tax after a house changes hands?
sections.html:
The seller stays liable for that year's bill. The county explains that whoever owned the parcel on January 1 carries the legal obligation, and a sale later in the year does not erase it.

Proration normally happens at closing, so confirm with your agent or closing attorney that it did. For certainty you can route the payment straight to the Tax Collector's Office at the table, and if the current bill is not yet due, the collector takes a prepayment computed at last year's rate.

State lien law reinforces this: the lien reaches the parcel on the listing date, as G.S. 105-355, and a buyer or lender will not accept title with it open. Once a closing date exists, ask the county tax office to put the amount owed in writing.

sections.h2: What steps does a Nash County assessment appeal follow?
sections.html:
The first stop is an informal appeal, and only a failed one leads to the county review board. No taxpayer may skip a step, says the county's revaluation page.

The informal step can be started four ways.

  • By appointment, face to face with an appraiser at the West Washington Street office in Nashville.
  • Over the phone, by arranging for an appraiser to call you.
  • By post: fill in the bottom of the appeal notice and send it with your documents to the Tax Office, marked for the Board of Equalization and Review.
  • On the web, using the county's informal appeal form.

Once the informal answer arrives, you get thirty days counted from the notice date to go formal, and you must prove the value is wrong. Under G.S. 105-322 the board convenes for the first time sometime from the first Monday of April to the first Monday of May.

The board weighs fairness and accuracy of the value, and the county's FAQ says it ignores whether you can afford the tax. Neighbors' comparable properties with lower assessments make the strongest evidence. A denial can move on to the Property Tax Commission, with notice due a month after the ruling goes out in the mail (G.S. 105-290).

sections.h2: Which relief programs does Nash County offer?
sections.html:
The county's Tax page names four: the elderly and permanently disabled exclusion, the disabled veterans' exclusion, the circuit breaker deferment and the builder's inventory exclusion. Request an application at (252) 459-1222 or download one from the tax forms page.

Key filing dates on the Nash County Tax page
ItemDeadline or rule
Elderly or disabled, disabled veterans, circuit breakerApplication due June 1
Builders' inventory and other reliefFiling due June 1
Other exemptions for classified parcels (Form AV-10)Filing due January 31
Personal and business personal property listingForms in hand by January 31, or a 10% late penalty
Property tax dueSeptember 1

The state revenue department lists $38,800 as the 2026 income limit for the elderly or disabled exclusion and circuit breaker, with $58,200 as the ceiling for the higher circuit breaker tier. For the elderly or disabled exclusion, a flat $25,000 or half the home's appraised value, whichever is greater, is taken off the assessment (G.S. 105-277.1), and a disabled veteran can exclude $45,000 of value, regardless of age or income.

sections.h2: How does a revaluation work in Nash County?
sections.html:
State law sets eight years as the longest gap between reappraisals, each effective January 1 of the scheduled year (G.S. 105-286). Nash County's own page describes the purpose as an accurate and equitable assessment of every parcel.

The county's revaluation page describes a project covering more than 53,000 parcels, carried out with an outside firm, Piner Appraisal, whose appraisers also take informal appeals. Each owner is mailed the new assessed value, and the thirty-day clock starts on the notice date.

The county defines market value as the price a willing, able buyer and seller would settle on with neither under pressure, and it excludes foreclosure and family sales. If your own sale was one of those, bring different comparables.

sections.h2: What else does the Nash County tax office handle besides real estate bills?
sections.html:
The collector's side of the office also deals with vehicles, business owners and utility customers, useful to know when you are closing out a household or a rental.

  • Bills for registered motor vehicles go out monthly instead of in the fall, and they have their own interest rule.
  • Business licenses are issued through the Tax Collector's Office.
  • Personal and business personal property forms must be in the office by the end of January, and a late listing carries a 10% penalty.
  • Check or cash payments for county water and sewer bills can be made at the Tax Collections Office in the administrative building in Nashville during regular business hours.

The county's Register of Deeds also sits in the same administrative building, on the third floor at 120 W. Washington Street, so a seller can record a deed and ask the tax office about a payoff in one trip.

faqs.q: What is the Nash County due date?
faqs.a: September 1 starts the payment period, and it runs through January 5 (extended past a weekend January 5). Interest of 2% then applies for January, followed by 0.75% each month.

faqs.q: If I sell partway through the year, do I still owe that year's tax?
faqs.a: Yes, unless it is settled at closing. The county treats whoever owned the parcel on January 1 as legally responsible, and a sale does not change that. Proration is typical, or you can pay the Tax Collector directly at the table.

faqs.q: How can I challenge my Nash County assessment?
faqs.a: Begin with an informal appeal, by phone, post, web form or in person. If the answer disappoints you, file a formal appeal with the Board of Equalization and Review thirty days after the date shown on the informal result.

faqs.q: When must Nash County relief applications arrive?
faqs.a: June 1 is the date for elderly or disabled, disabled veteran, circuit breaker and builders' inventory applications. Classified-parcel exemptions on Form AV-10 are due January 31.

faqs.q: How steep is the Nash County late listing penalty?
faqs.a: It is 10%. Personal and business personal property forms must reach the county by January 31, and late ones carry that penalty as the law requires.
